introduction: This spec rewrites the carry-patch workflow guide, the agent-instructions example and ADR 01 so they describe the two patch-branch authority models (hub and origin) delivered by specs 20 to 23. It also records ADR 01 as accepted, files errata for each divergence from the original proposal, and adds a documentation test. It changes no code behaviour.

glossary.authority model: The choice of which git copy of a patch branch is the writer of record: the hub's own git server (hub mode) or the fork named origin (origin mode), selected by the workspace variable PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE.
glossary.docs test: A Go test in internal/carrypatch/docs_test.go that asserts content of documentation files, using the readDoc, requireContains and section helpers.
glossary.erratum: A file under docs/errata/ named NN_snake_case_topic.md with the sections Spec Expectation, Implementation Reality and Resolution, recording where delivered behaviour differs from what was specified.
glossary.fork: The user's GitHub copy of the upstream repository, configured as the git remote origin of the workspace trunk.
glossary.hub: The agent-fox hub service, which hosts a git server per workspace and rebuilds the integration branch from patch branches.
glossary.origin_sync_state: Per-patch sync state recorded in origin mode: in_sync, diverged or missing_on_origin.
glossary.patch branch: A branch holding one carry patch, registered in the workspace with afc patch add.
glossary.replaced backup ref: refs/hub/replaced/<branch>, the hub-side ref that keeps the previous tip of a patch branch when sync replaces it with the fork's tip.
glossary.trunk: The hub's bare clone of the workspace repository; a rebuild reads patch branches only from refs/heads/<branch> in it.

criteria.condition: the shipped code of specs 20 to 23 differs from a spec PRD in a detail the documents describe
criteria.action: describe the behaviour of the code and record the difference as an entry in the erratum file of the delivering spec
criteria.contract: the guide text matches the code; the erratum file for that spec lists the divergence with its reason

criteria.condition: a behaviour claim cannot be found in the shipped code or in a test
criteria.action: omit the claim from the rewritten documents
criteria.contract: no sentence in the guide, agent example or ADR 01 asserts a behaviour that has no code or test evidence

criteria.action: modify only documentation files and internal/carrypatch/docs_test.go, leaving code, routes, CLI commands, variables and schemas unchanged

requirements.title: Remotes table and the "Where patch branches live" section
requirements.rationale: The guide must stop implying that origin always holds patch branches, because the code reads only the trunk's refs/heads/<branch>.

criteria.action: describe origin as the fork, the push target for the integration branch (REBUILD_PUSH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH) and, in origin mode, the authority for patch branches, and not contain the string "Where patch branches live; push target for local work"
name the hub's own git server, through a third row or a note, as the place patch branches are written in hub mode

contain a section headed "Where patch branches live" after Concepts/Remotes that states a rebuild reads only refs/heads/<branch> in the workspace trunk and that the initial clone brings the fork's branches in only as refs/remotes/origin/*

explain PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE with the values hub (default) and origin, and include a comparison table with the rows: who writes the branch, what sync does with it, what registration does, what a push to the hub does (reject, forward with PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN=true, or accept and optionally mirror), what happens on divergence, where a person fixes a conflict, and which copy survives a lost hub data directory

recommend origin mode with REBUILD_PUSH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH=true for teams that open upstream pull requests, recommend hub mode for agent-driven workspaces that never open upstream PRs, and state that the integration branch is always built by the hub, only pushed to the fork and never fetched from origin by sync

state that the mode is read at the start of each operation, and include a switching-modes note: switching to origin makes the next sync bring registered branches to the fork's tips (previous hub tips kept under refs/hub/replaced/<branch>), and switching to hub stops fork fetches and clears persisted origin sync state at the next sync
point to the Configuration section for PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE, PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY and PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN

criteria.action: list origin_sync_state, origin_sha and origin_synced_at, stating each is absent when null and written only in origin mode

explain the sync states in_sync, diverged and missing_on_origin, and state that missing_on_origin leaves the patch status unchanged so the rebuild keeps applying the hub's copy until an operator disables or removes the patch

criteria.system: guide registration text (Getting Started "Add patches" and "Adding a new patch")
criteria.action: describe the resolution order refs/heads/<name>, refs/remotes/origin/<name>, then (origin mode only) a single-branch fork fetch, quote the 400 message "branch does not exist in repository or on origin", state that a fork-only branch no longer needs --skip-branch-check, and state that --skip-branch-check is for branches that exist nowhere yet
state that the backup ref refs/hub/replaced/<branch> is deleted with the patch row and that the branch itself is not deleted

criteria.system: guide soft-delete and "Restoring a soft-deleted patch" text
criteria.action: state the 7-day retention window

criteria.contract: no sentence in the guide says a background purge or scheduler removes expired patches after 7 days

criteria.action: describe the purge schedule exactly as the code implements it

requirements.title: Getting Started: fork-first walkthrough with hub alternative
requirements.rationale: The recommended path for teams that open upstream pull requests is fork-authoritative, and the walkthrough must show that sync, not rebuild, brings fork commits into the hub.

criteria.action: present the primary walkthrough on acme-oss/api-gateway and your-org/api-gateway-fork in this order: create workspace, set upstream credentials (unchanged), choose the authority, push a patch branch to the fork, register it, sync, then the existing preview, manual rebuild, dashboard, failed-rebuild and rollback steps renumbered

show afc vars create PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE=origin --workspace api-gateway, optionally with REBUILD_PUSH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH=true, and state that a fork clone and a fork token with read access are needed on every sync via the workspace's GIT_PAT or GIT_USERNAME/GIT_PASSWORD

criteria.system: guide fork-first steps for branch creation and registration
criteria.action: show creating the patch branch in a normal clone of the fork, pushing it to the fork, opening the upstream PR from the same branch, and registering with afc patch add without --skip-branch-check, keeping the existing position, --if-not-exists and batch examples

show afc workspace sync api-gateway and explain that in origin mode sync, not afc rebuild submit, brings new fork commits into the hub because a rebuild reads the hub's copy of each branch and does not fetch the fork

show a sample response containing origin_fetched, patches_synced and patches_diverged next to the existing fields, and cover the outcomes created, fast_forwarded and replaced, the --fail-on-diverged flag with exit code 3, and PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY
mention the per-patch sync-state fields and the new summary counts

contain a heading "Alternative: hub-authoritative workspace" showing: leave PATCH_BRANCH_SOURCE unset, push the branch to the hub's git URL, register, let the push hook rebuild or run afc rebuild submit, optionally set PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN=true to mirror accepted pushes to the fork, and state this flow suits agent-driven workspaces
use only afc commands and flags that exist in docs/cli.md

requirements.title: Sync, push and rebuild-trigger text
requirements.rationale: The sync section must match the sync spec 20 delivers, or the recommended workflow would silently rebuild stale patch tips.

criteria.action: describe in order: credential resolution and the upstream fetch; the origin fetch (origin mode only); base resolution; the patch refresh; force-push detection; merge detection (also run when only patch tips changed); the rebuild decision; and the unconditional write of last_sync_at
state that the origin fetch prunes stale tracking refs and that its failure answers "502 origin fetch failed" and leaves all refs and patch state unchanged
describe the patch refresh outcomes created, fast_forwarded and replaced, the states in_sync, diverged and missing_on_origin, and the backup ref refs/hub/replaced/<branch>

state that a rebuild is triggered when upstream advanced, an active or conflict patch moved, or a patch was newly merged, unless AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC=false, and that the AUTO_REBUILD_AFTER_SYNC entry covers patch changes as well as upstream advances

criteria.condition: the guide contains a statement that sync returns immediately when upstream is unchanged
criteria.action: remove the statement and the interim two-models note written by spec 20, without keeping both
criteria.contract: the guide contains no sentence that sync returns immediately on an unchanged upstream and exactly one description of the two models, in "Where patch branches live"

criteria.action: keep the push hook description and add how a push to a registered patch branch is treated in each mode (rejection in origin mode, forwarding with PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN=true, mirroring in hub mode) and that only accepted ref updates trigger the hook
stay unchanged apart from one added sentence that the patch tips it snapshots are whatever the last sync (origin mode) or push (hub mode) left in the trunk

requirements.title: Conflict resolution and divergence recovery in both modes
requirements.rationale: Telling an origin-mode operator to edit the trunk or push to the hub would have the fix rejected, forwarded or overwritten.

criteria.system: guide "Resolving conflicts after a failed rebuild" section and the Getting Started failed-rebuild step
criteria.action: each open with a common part (read conflict_files in afc workspace patch-status) followed by one subsection for hub mode and one for origin mode

keep the existing instructions (resolve in the trunk or push a fixed branch to the hub's git server, set the patch to active, rebuild), say rerere records the resolution when it happens during a rebuild, and state what the code supports for manual rerere recording

instruct: fix the branch in a local clone (merge or rebase the latest upstream, resolve, commit), push it to the fork, run afc workspace sync, and set the patch back to active if its status is still conflict after the rebuild

criteria.condition: a reader of the origin mode subsection looks for the place to apply a fix
criteria.action: tell the reader not to edit the trunk and not to push to the hub, and give the reason (a hub push is rejected, forwarded or replaced, and a trunk edit is overwritten at the next sync)
criteria.contract: the origin mode subsection contains no instruction to edit the trunk or push to the hub other than that prohibition

criteria.action: state as a known limitation, not a planned feature, that a resolution made on the fork is not recorded in the hub's rerere cache, so the same conflict is resolved by hand again unless the rebuild itself resolves it

contain a section "Recovering a replaced or diverged patch branch" covering reading origin_sync_state and replaced_sha, fetching a replaced tip with git fetch <hub_url> refs/hub/replaced/<branch>, and pushing it to the fork to keep it

describe afc patch reset-to-origin <slug> <patch-id> moving a diverged branch to the fork's tip and reporting rebuild_triggered, state that only one backup per branch exists and later replacements overwrite it, and say what to do with missing_on_origin

criteria.action: state the default (hub, replace and unset), the exact-match rule, that PATCH_DIVERGENCE_POLICY is ignored in hub mode, and that PUSH_PATCHES_TO_ORIGIN means forwarding in origin mode and mirroring in hub mode
include a table of recommended combinations with four rows: fork-first (origin, optional REBUILD_PUSH_INTEGRATION_BRANCH=true), fork-first with hub forwarding, hub-only, and hub with a durable mirror
